title: Choose the app's structure
question: Aether keeps its look (The Typeset Proof); this choice is how the workspace, library, guide and settings fit together. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The Margin Auditor
options.thesis: The proof fills the page; each line's verdict sits in a margin column aligned to that very line.
options.viewport: A slim left rail (Workspace, Library, Guide, Settings) and file tree; one wide sheet with source on the left and a ruled margin on the right where each statement's status and reason sit level with its line; the context state opens as a drawer under the selected line; a status bar along the foot.
options.risk: Long explanations must wrap in a narrow margin; very wide screens are needed for comfort.

options.label: The Proof Sheet
options.lineage: a typeset proof with the referee's notes set under each line
options.thesis: One reading column per file: every statement followed directly by its verdict and reason, like a referee's annotated proof.
options.viewport: A top bar with file tabs and the view switcher; a centred column where you edit the proof and verdicts appear interleaved under the lines that earn them; the context state and library open as side sheets; the explorer is a collapsible left sheet.
options.risk: Interleaving moves lines as verdicts arrive, which can jolt the caret while typing.

options.label: Notes Beside the Proof
options.lineage: lecture notes open next to a working sheet
options.thesis: A study desk: the course-pack entry or guide page stays open on the left while you write and check the proof on the right.
options.viewport: A left rail of views; a reading pane showing the library entry ("Example 2.18", its statement, hints) or a guide section; a working pane with editor tabs, the auditor beneath and the context state as a collapsible strip; a status bar along the foot.
options.risk: Two reading surfaces compete on small laptops; the reading pane must collapse cleanly.
